st: Combine the chicken, [[0.5 cup]] soy sauce, [[0.5 cup]] vinegar, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns in a bowl.
Marinate for 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Move the chicken and marinade to a pot, add [[0.5 cup]] water and bring to a boil without stirring.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, turning the chicken once, until it reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the chicken and pat dry. Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and brown the chicken for 3 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, boil the sauce uncovered for 8 minutes until reduced and glossy. Add [[1 tsp]] sugar if you like.
Return the chicken to the sauce, coat well and serve with steamed rice.
Put the pork in a pot with [[8 cups]] water and bring to a boil.
Skim off the foam for the first few minutes.
Add the onion and tomatoes, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] tamarind paste and [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce.
Add the radish and cook 8 minutes.
Add the green beans and peppers and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook 2 minutes until wilted.
Taste, add salt if needed, and serve hot with rice.

ing: pork belly or boneless pork shoulder with skin
st: Pat the pork dry. Pierce the skin all over with a skewer or fork.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce with the pepper and rub it into the meat side only.
Lay the pork skin-side up and rub [[3 tbsp]] salt on the skin. Chill uncovered overnight for dry, crisp skin.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Brush off the extra salt.
Arrange the lemongrass, garlic, onions and green onions on the meat side and roll or fold the pork tightly, tying with kitchen string.
Brush the skin with [[2 tbsp]] oil. Roast on a rack for 2 hours 30 minutes.
Raise the oven to 475°F (245°C) and roast 20 to 30 minutes until the skin blisters and crackles. Watch carefully so it does not burn.
Rest for 20 minutes. The center should reach at least 145°F (63°C).
Chop with a heavy knife and serve with liver sauce or vinegar dip.

ing: flour stick noodles or chow mein
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large wok over medium-high heat.
Cook the garlic and onion for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 5 minutes until cooked through to 165°F (74°C).
Add the shrimp and cook 2 minutes until pink.
Add the carrots and cabbage and cook 3 minutes.
Pour in [[1.5 cups]] broth, [[3 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] oyster sauce and the pepper and bring to a simmer.
Add the noodles and toss, cooking 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles are tender.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.
Mix the pork, carrot, onion, garlic, 1 egg, [[1 tbsp]] soy sauce, salt and pepper until well combined.
Cook a small test spoonful in a pan and taste, then adjust the seasoning.
Lay a wrapper in a diamond shape and place [[2 tbsp]] filling near one corner.
Fold the corner over, tuck in the sides, and roll up tightly.
Seal the end with beaten egg.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and the pork inside reaches 160°F (71°C).
Drain on paper towels and serve with sweet chili sauce.
Place the oxtail in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water and bring to a boil, skimming foam.
Simmer covered for 2 hours 30 minutes until the meat is tender.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil with annatto for 2 minutes, then discard the seeds and keep the colored oil.
Cook the onion and garlic in the colored oil for 4 minutes.
Stir the onion mixture into the pot with [[0.5 cup]] peanut butter.
Whisk [[0.25 cup]] rice flour with some broth and stir in to thicken for 10 minutes.
Add eggplant and beans and cook 6 minutes, then add bok choy for 2 minutes.
Season with [[1 tsp]] salt and serve with rice and [[2 tbsp]] shrimp paste on the side.

ing: raw yolk cooked on the hot plate, optional
st: Boil the pork belly in salted water for 40 minutes until tender and it reaches at least 145°F (63°C).
Drain and pat dry, then grill or broil for 8 minutes per side until the skin is crisp.
Chop the pork into very small pieces.
Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Add the pork and onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chili, [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[0.25 cup]] calamansi juice and pepper and stir.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] mayonnaise off the heat.
Make a small well, crack in the egg and let it cook on the hot pan, mixing in at the table.
Serve sizzling with extra lime.

ing: peeled, seeded and cut in wedges; or use chayote
st: Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pot and cook the garlic, onion and ginger for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Pour in [[3 tbsp]] fish sauce and cook 1 minute.
Add [[6 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Add the papaya and simmer 10 minutes until tender.
Check that the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part.
Stir in the spinach and pepper and cook 2 minutes.
Serve hot in bowls with steamed rice.
Mix [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce, [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, pepper and 6 minced garlic cloves in a bowl.
Add the beef and marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and fry the 4 remaining minced garlic cloves until golden.
Add the rice and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and stir-fry for 5 minutes. Keep warm.
Cook the beef with its marinade in a hot pan for 6 minutes until the liquid cooks off and the edges brown.
Wipe the pan, heat [[3 tbsp]] oil and fry the eggs to your liking.
Serve the beef with garlic rice and a fried egg on each plate.
Chill four tall glasses in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Spoon a tablespoon of red beans, coconut and ube jam into each glass.
Add one slice of leche flan to each glass.
Fill each glass with shaved ice, mounding it high.
Pour [[0.25 cup]] cold evaporated milk over each glass.
Sprinkle [[1.5 tsp]] sugar over each if you like.
Top with a scoop of ube ice cream.
Serve right away and mix everything together before eating.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C) and boil a kettle of water.
Melt [[0.5 cup]] sugar in a small saucepan over medium heat until amber. Pour into an 8-inch round pan or llanera and tilt to coat the bottom.
Whisk the yolks gently with the condensed milk, evaporated milk, lime zest and vanilla without making foam.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into the caramel pan.
Cover the pan tightly with a sheet of foil.
Set the pan in a larger tray and pour hot water halfway up the sides.
Bake for 55 minutes until set with a slight wobble in the center.
Cool, then chill at least 4 hours.
Run a knife around the edge and invert onto a plate.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Soften banana leaves over a flame and line two 8-inch cake pans.
Whisk [[1.5 cups]] rice flour, [[1 tbsp]] baking powder and [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
In another bowl whisk the eggs, [[0.75 cup]] sugar, [[1 cup]] coconut milk and [[3 tbsp]] melted butter.
Combine the wet and dry mixtures until smooth.
Pour into the pans and bake for 15 minutes.
Scatter cheese on top and bake 10 minutes more until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Brush with remaining melted butter and finish with coconut.
Serve warm, straight from the pan.
Whisk the milk, sugar and yeast together and rest 5 minutes until foamy.
Add the flour, salt, butter and egg. Mix, then knead for 10 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 60 minutes until doubled.
Roll the dough into a log about 14 inches long and cut into 12 equal pieces. Roll each piece in breadcrumbs.
Place the rolls cut-side up on a lined tray, 2 inches apart. Cover and rise 30 minutes until puffy.
Bake at 375°F for 15 minutes until golden brown. Serve warm with butter or cheese.
nt: Baked at 375°F
Best swap: use plant milk and vegan butter in the same amounts, and replace the egg with 3 tbsp plant milk.

st: Peel the bananas and cut each in half lengthwise to make 6 pieces. Roll each piece in about [[0.5 tbsp]] brown sugar to coat.
Lay a wrapper in a diamond shape. Place a banana piece and a few jackfruit strips near the bottom corner.
Fold the bottom corner over the filling, fold in both sides, and roll tightly. Dab the last corner with a little water to seal. Make 6 rolls.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 340°F, about 1 inch deep. A scrap of wrapper should sizzle at once.
Fry 3 rolls at a time, turning, for 3 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain on a rack or paper towels.
Pour off all but [[1 tbsp]] oil. Add [[0.5 cup]] brown sugar and let it melt and bubble without stirring for 2 minutes until deep amber.
Roll the fried turon in the caramel quickly, then place on parchment for 2 minutes until the glaze hardens. Serve warm.
nt: Deep-fried at 340°F, then caramel-glazed
Best swap: firm ripe plantains for saba bananas, and bake at 400°F for 20 minutes with oil brushed on if you do not want to deep fry.

st: Open the fruit cocktail and pineapple and drain them in a colander for at least 10 minutes. Press lightly with the back of a spoon so the cream will not turn watery.
Drain the nata de coco and kaong, rinse them quickly under water to remove the syrup, and drain them well again.
In a large bowl, mix [[1 cup]] chilled all-purpose cream with [[0.5 cup]] condensed milk until smooth and pale.
Fold in the drained fruit cocktail, pineapple, nata de coco, kaong and coconut strips, using a spatula and turning gently so the fruit pieces stay whole.
Add the cheddar cubes if you like the sweet and salty contrast; many families do this for fiestas and Noche Buena.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, until the cream is cold and thick. Taste and add a bit more condensed milk if needed.
Spoon into a chilled bowl or small cups and top with the cherries. Serve very cold.
nt: Don't cook: mix and chill
Best swap: fresh mango and ripe cantaloupe cubes for the canned fruit cocktail, and coconut cream with sugar for dairy-free cream.

ing: about 1 lb each, deboned and butterflied
st: Rub the open fish inside and out with [[2 tbsp]] calamansi juice, garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Rest 15 minutes.
Mix the tomatoes, onion and ginger. Stuff the mixture into the cavity of each fish, then close and tie with kitchen twine or secure with skewers.
Wrap each fish loosely in a banana leaf if using, which keeps the skin intact and adds aroma.
Heat charcoal or a grill to medium, about 375°F. Grill the fish 10 minutes on the first side without moving.
Turn once and grill 8 to 10 minutes more until the flesh reads 145°F and the skin is charred in spots.
Serve with steamed rice and a dipping sauce of [[0.25 cup]] vinegar with chopped chilies and garlic.
nt: Grilled over medium coals, stuffed and slow-cooked
Best swap: wrap in foil and bake at 400°F for 25 minutes. Use whole tilapia or trout for milkfish.

st: Chill the coconuts in the fridge for a few hours beforehand so the water tastes clean and cold.
Hack off the top of each coconut with a heavy knife, or cut a hole, and pour the water into a pitcher. You should get about [[2 cups]] total.
Split the coconuts open and scrape out the soft, jelly-like meat with a spoon. Slice into thin ribbons.
Stir the calamansi juice into the coconut water. Add [[2 tbsp]] sugar only if the coconuts are not sweet.
Divide the meat among glasses, add ice, and pour the coconut water over. Serve with a spoon.
nt: Don't cook: crack, scrape and mix over ice
Best swap: no fresh buko, use 2 cups bottled coconut water and 1 cup frozen young coconut strips.

st: Mix the flour, warm milk, yeast, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, yolks and a pinch of salt. Knead in [[0.5 cup]] butter and work 12 minutes until smooth and silky.
Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 10 pieces and roll each into a long rope about 12 inches. Coil each into a spiral in a greased muffin cup or paper mold.
Cover and rise 1 hour more until very puffy. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes until golden. Brush at once with the soft butter while hot.
Sprinkle with [[0.33 cup]] sugar and the grated cheddar while still warm so the topping clings.
nt: Baked at 350°F
Best swap: use queso de bola or Edam for the cheddar, or vegan butter and oat milk for a dairy-free version.

st: Poke the eggplants a few times with a fork. Char them over a gas flame or under a broiler, turning, for 10 to 15 minutes until the skin is blackened and the flesh collapses.
Place the eggplants in a bowl, cover and rest 5 minutes so the skin loosens.
Peel off the skin, keeping the stem on if you like, and lay the flesh on a plate. Press gently with a fork to flatten.
Mix the tomatoes and red onion with [[3 tbsp]] vinegar, [[1 tbsp]] fish sauce, [[1 tsp]] sugar and pepper.
Spoon the topping over the eggplant and add the diced salted egg if using. Serve with grilled fish or fried pork.
nt: Charred over open flame or under the broiler
Best swap: soy sauce plus a squeeze of lime in place of fish sauce for a vegetarian version.

st: Crack open a young coconut, pour its water into a measuring cup, and scrape out the soft meat with a spoon. You need [[1 cup]] meat and [[1 cup]] water.
Put the meat, water, [[0.5 cup]] evaporated milk and [[2 tbsp]] sugar in a blender.
Blend on high for 40 seconds until the coconut is mostly smooth with only tiny flecks left.
Add [[1.5 cup]] crushed ice and blend another 20 seconds until thick and slushy.
Taste, add a little more sugar if needed, and pour into tall glasses. Serve right away with a wide straw.
nt: Don't cook: just blend
Best swap: use frozen young coconut meat and bottled coconut water, and replace evaporated milk with coconut milk.

st: Peel the bananas and cut them in half crosswise if they are long. Push a skewer through the length of each piece.
Pour the oil into a deep heavy pot, at least 2 inches deep, and heat it to 350°F.
Spread [[0.5 cup]] brown sugar on a plate and roll each banana in it so it is well coated all over.
Carefully lower 2 or 3 bananas into the oil. Fry for 2 minutes, turning, until the sugar melts into a dark amber caramel and the bananas are golden.
Add a pinch of the remaining sugar to the oil if the caramel is not forming; this speeds the coating.
Lift out with tongs and rest on a rack for 2 minutes. The caramel hardens as it cools. Serve warm.
nt: Deep-fried at 350°F
Best swap: plain ripe plantains work 1 to 1 for saba bananas; a firm cooking banana is better than a soft dessert banana.

st: Put the longganisa and [[0.5 cup]] water in a skillet over medium heat. Cover and simmer 10 minutes until the water is gone.
Uncover and fry the sausages in their own fat for 5 minutes, turning until caramelized. Pork must reach 160°F inside.
In a wok, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil on medium. Fry the garlic 1 minute until just golden; do not let it go dark.
Add the rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry for 4 minutes. Season with salt.
Fry the eggs in [[1 tbsp]] oil until the whites are set and the edges are crisp. Cook until yolks are set to your liking.
Plate the garlic rice with the sausages and egg, with tomato and a small dish of [[0.25 cup]] vinegar for dipping.
nt: Simmered then pan-fried; garlic rice stir-fried
Best swap: any sweet breakfast sausage or Chinese lap cheong for longganisa, same count.

st: Mix both flours with the salt. Add the water a little at a time, rubbing with your fingers until it looks like damp, crumbly sand that holds together when squeezed.
Make steaming tubes: roll oiled foil around a thick marker to make 6 tubes about 5 inches long, then slide out the marker. Grease the insides with oil.
Pack each tube loosely with the dough, filling it to the top.
Bring water to a boil in a steamer. Stand the tubes upright on a steamer rack, cover, and steam for 12 to 15 minutes until the dough is firm and sticky.
Slide the cooked sticks out of the tubes onto a platter while hot. Be careful: the steam burns.
Brush each stick with butter. Roll in the coconut, then sprinkle thickly with the muscovado sugar. Serve warm.
nt: Steamed in tubes over boiling water
Best swap: use all regular glutinous rice flour plus 1 tsp ube extract for the purple rice flour.

st: Put the pork belly in a pot with water to cover, the bay leaves, peppercorns, garlic, onion and [[2 tbsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer and cook covered for 50 minutes until a knife slides in with little resistance. Skim off foam at the start.
Lift the pork out, pat very dry and refrigerate uncovered on a rack for 1 hour. A dry skin blisters and crackles.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] vinegar, [[0.25 cup]] soy sauce and the red onion for the dip. Set aside.
Heat [[6 cup]] oil in a deep heavy pot to 375°F. Cut the belly in 2 pieces first and lower in away from you, as the oil spits. Cover with a splatter screen.
Fry for 8 minutes, turning once, until the skin is blistered, golden and crisp. Drain on a rack.
Rest 5 minutes. Chop into bite-size pieces with a heavy knife and serve with the dip and rice.
nt: Simmered tender, then deep-fried until crackling
Best swap: air-fry the dried boiled belly at 400°F for 25 minutes instead of deep frying, using far less oil.

st: Simmer the shrimp shells and heads in [[3 cup]] water for 15 minutes. Strain, discard the shells, and keep the stock.
Soak the annatto seeds in [[0.25 cup]] hot water for 10 minutes, rub them to release the color, and strain the orange water.
Cook the shrimp in boiling water for 2 minutes until pink. Remove, cool, and peel if not yet peeled.
Heat the oil and cook half the garlic with the ground pork over medium heat until no pink remains, about 6 minutes.
Whisk the flour into the strained annatto water and stock, then pour into the pork. Add the fish sauce and simmer 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Soak the rice noodles in hot water for 8 minutes until pliable, then boil for 2 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Pile the noodles on a platter, pour the sauce over, and top with shrimp, egg, chicharron, scallions and fried garlic. Serve with calamansi.
nt: Boiled noodles, thickened simmered sauce
Best swap: use 1 tbsp paprika with a pinch of turmeric if you cannot find annatto; lemon plus a little lime works for calamansi.

st: Toss the shredded papaya with [[1 tbsp]] salt and massage for 2 minutes. Rest for 30 minutes.
Squeeze out as much liquid as possible, using a clean towel or cheesecloth, and discard the liquid. This keeps the pickle crunchy.
In a pot, combine [[1.5 cups]] vinegar, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water and [[1 tbsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, stirring until dissolved, then cool completely.
Mix the papaya, carrot, pepper, ginger, garlic, onion and [[0.25 cup]] raisins in a bowl.
Pack tightly into clean jars and pour the cooled brine over to cover completely. Press down to release trapped air.
Seal and refrigerate for at least 3 days (best 1 week) before serving beside fried fish, grilled pork or longganisa.
nt: Salted, then cold-pickled in sweet brine; rests 3 or more days
Best swap: unripe green mango or kohlrabi for green papaya in the same quantity, and white vinegar for cane vinegar.

st: Heat a little oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, minced garlic and ginger 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and brown 4 minutes per side. Stir in [[2 tbsp]] fish sauce.
Add both rices and the turmeric and stir 1 minute. Pour in [[6 cup]] stock and bring to a boil.
Simmer on low 35 minutes, stirring often, until the chicken is tender (165°F) and the rice is thick and creamy.
Shred the chicken off the bones and return it to the pot. Add water if too thick.
Fry the remaining sliced garlic in oil until golden. Ladle the arroz caldo into bowls and top with eggs, garlic, scallions and calamansi.
nt: Simmered slowly to a porridge
Best swap: use all jasmine rice if you have no glutinous rice; stir more to thicken.
